_comment: Paraphyletic grades. A grade is not a clade and must not be drawn as one, so
the app renders these as a bracket spanning a set of successive stem branches
rather than as a collapsible triangle.
members    resolved from fossils.json: any fossil listing this grade id.
paraphyletic  true for a grade proper. A few entries here are clades whose
*named* content is paraphyletic -- Theropoda is a clade, but
'non-avian theropods' is what the fossils on that stem are.
excludes   the living clade the grade is defined by excluding. This is what
makes the paraphyly explicit rather than implied.
Grades may nest: Dimetrodon is a pelycosaur, a non-mammalian synapsid, and
neither of those is a clade.

grades.label: "ostracoderms"
grades.note: Armoured jawless stem gnathostomes. Not a clade: each of these lineages branches off the same stem at a different point, and Osteostraci is closer to you than it is to Pteraspidomorphi. The name survives because the animals look alike, which is exactly the trap.

grades.label: "placoderms"
grades.note: Armoured jawed fishes of the Silurian and Devonian. Read as a clade until Entelognathus turned up in 2013 with bony-fish jaw margins. Now generally a grade on the gnathostome stem, with different placoderms closer to different living groups. The placoderm-monophyly toggle restores the older arrangement.

grades.label: "acanthodians"
grades.note: "Spiny sharks", which were neither especially spiny by placoderm standards nor sharks. Braincase evidence from Acanthodes moved them onto the chondrichthyan stem as a grade.

grades.label: "palaeoniscoids"
grades.note: Early ray-finned fishes, grouped by retained ancestral characters and nothing else. A textbook wastebasket.

grades.label: stem tetrapods
grades.note: The fish-tetrapod transition. Reading down this ladder from Eusthenopteron to Tulerpeton is reading the acquisition of limbs, necks and weight-bearing joints one branch at a time, in animals that were all still aquatic.

grades.label: non-mammalian synapsids
grades.note: Once called "mammal-like reptiles", which is wrong twice: they are not reptiles, and calling them mammal-like implies they are approximations of mammals rather than their own animals. Synapsida is a clade; the non-mammalian part of it is not.

grades.label: "pelycosaurs"
grades.note: Early synapsids excluding therapsids. Dimetrodon is the one everyone can draw, and it is neither a dinosaur nor a reptile.

grades.label: non-mammalian cynodonts
grades.note: Where the jaw joint migrates and the middle ear is assembled out of the bones that used to hinge the jaw.

grades.label: stem turtles
grades.note: The shell assembles in stages: broadened ribs, then a plastron, then a carapace, then a retractable neck. Each stage is a separate branch.

grades.label: non-crocodylian pseudosuchians
grades.note: The crocodile-line archosaurs. For most of the Triassic these, not dinosaurs, were the dominant large land vertebrates.

grades.label: non-avian dinosaurs
grades.note: Dinosauria is a clade and birds are in it. "Non-avian dinosaurs" is the grade you get by cutting the birds out, and it is the group that ends at the K-Pg boundary.

grades.label: non-avian coelurosaurs
grades.note: Feathers, wishbones, brooding and hollow bones are all present down here, before flight and before birds.

grades.label: stem birds (Avialae)
grades.note: From Archaeopteryx to Ichthyornis. Every one of these is a bird by most people's definition and none of them is a crown bird.

grades.label: extinct in historical time
grades.note: Not a grade at all, a flag. These lineages are scattered across the tree and every one of them was lost after written records began. Grouped so the pattern is visible in one click.
